newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Diffs firm slightly as prices dip.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Diffs firm slightly as prices dip.

text.p: U.S. refined product prices weakened again Friday as the NYMEX continued its downward path, though differentials firmed modestly during the first half of the day.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline was down 1.02 cent at 60.15 cents and July heating oil was down 0.62 cent at 54.00 cents.
U.S. GULF
Conventional unleaded gasoline spot differentials rose in the U.S. Gulf as refiners bought supplies to meet a shipping deadline on the Colonial Pipeline.
"This all has to do with the shipping deadline. There is no other news out there," said a U.S. Gulf trader.
Conventional unleaded M1 was offered at 0.90 cent under NYMEX July gasoline versus 1.00 cent Thursday.

Low sulphur diesel traded in line with Thursday's values with a deal done at 1.75 cents under NYMEX July heating oil. The bid/ask spread narrowed for low sulphur diesel at 1.80 to 1.65 under versus 1.90 to 1.65 under Thursday, paving the way for stronger prices, dealers said.
The heating oil futures prices are becoming more indicative of spot supply, so the difference to the spot prices is narrowing, dealers said.
"Differentials are strengthening as a result of the fall in the outright price which is reflecting the supply situation more," said a dealer.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Differentials at New York Harbor showed little movement early Friday, with few active buyers emerging.
Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline was talked between 2.00 and 2.25 cents under the July NYMEX, even with late Thursday levels, according to traders.
Prompt reformulated 87-octane gasoline was quoted between 0.25 and 0.50 cent over the July NYMEX, slightly above prices seen late Thursday, but still off the strength seen earlier this week.

Reformulated gasoline barrels remained in ample supply in the Harbor, with traders citing the more than one-million-barrel delivery BP is set to receive, as well as the steady flow of imports into the East Coast.
MIDCONTINENT
The Midcontinent markets were called quiet on Friday although pre-weekend deals were getting done to push differentials up about a quarter cent.

Group Three prompt unleaded differentials rose a quarter to between 4.50 cents and 4.75 cents over July NYMEX. Prompt 4.75 cents parcels were done amid a one-day decrease in days of supply along the Williams pipeline system, traders said.
Chicago market unleaded gasoline differentials were also stronger, with barrels trading at 4.00 cents over the print.
"With the Merc down there is some buying going on before the weekend," said a products trader.
Low sulphur and premium in both hubs were also a tad stronger, with low sulphur differentials pegged 4.00 to 4.50 cents over July heating oil in Group Three.
